artifacts.summary: Phase 3 (vendor delegation with single-writer normalization) completed; records the delegated/HTTP byte-identity design, the deployed-mirror verify-touched.sh staleness caveat (carried forward), and the host's own vendor client genuinely predating link support.

next_steps: Dispatch Phase 4 (/sapience Pick Surface) of the same plan; Phase 5 depends on both 3 and 4.

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented Phase 3 of 5: bind mode now delegates its --confirm registration to the installed vendor client's own `link` subcommand when statically detected as supported (python3 "$SAPIENCE_CLI_PATH" link <value> --name <repo_slug>), reading the vendor's written file back and re-rendering it through write_link_file() so this script remains the sole, canonical writer either way; any non-success vendor outcome falls through to Phase 2's own HTTP path unchanged. Added test cases 22-24 against a synthetic sapience_cli.py fixture (never the real installation); all 24 cases (61 assertions) pass against the source store.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan requires that a delegated subprocess's own written output file become the canonical artifact (never the delegate's raw serialization), read the file back by its own declared keys and re-render through the same single-writer helper the non-delegated path already uses, rather than trusting the delegate's bytes directly. This turns 'byte-identical on either path' into a structurally enforced invariant (both paths funnel through one writer) instead of a hope about two independently-maintained serializers staying in sync.

To test a byte-identity requirement between two independently-constructed code paths that each embed a basename-derived value (e.g. a cwd-derived repo slug) in their output, build the two scratch fixtures with a fixed, shared leaf directory name (via mkdir under two different mktemp -d parents) rather than two independent mktemp -d calls -- this keeps the basename-derived field identical across both paths without weakening the comparison to 'ignore that one field', so a whole-file cmp remains a meaningful, exact proof.

sapience_notes.subject: Vendor CLI delegation detection must be static, never a live probe
sapience_notes.value: The sapience CLI binary on $PATH (a NixOS-packaged wrapper) cannot be used to detect or invoke a vendor client's `link` subcommand at all: it dispatches via a fixed case table with no `link` branch and no fallback into the underlying sapience_cli.py's own argument parser, so invoking it for 'link' fails regardless of what the Python file underneath actually supports. Detection must grep the Python source file directly (grep -q "sub == 'link'") and invocation must go straight at `python3 "$SAPIENCE_CLI_PATH" link ...`, bypassing the $PATH wrapper entirely. Confirmed live: this machine's installed ~/.sapience/sapience_cli.py (1122 lines) genuinely predates `link` support and falls through to a generic usage printout with no network call.

sapience_notes.subject: Reconciling a delegation requirement with a 'write anyway on 404' requirement
sapience_notes.value: Pure delegation to a vendor CLI cannot satisfy a '404 still writes the file in a degraded state' requirement when the vendor's own CLI writes nothing on 404. The resolution that preserves both requirements: delegate only the write-and-register call itself, and only when the vendor client exits 0 with a link file actually present on disk; read that file's own keys back and re-render them through the single-writer helper that already handles the create and non-delegated bind paths. Any other vendor outcome (non-zero exit, or exit 0 with no file) falls through unchanged to the script's own HTTP path, which alone implements the 404/403 status-code policy. Accepted consequence: against a link-capable client, a 404 or 403 outcome causes both the vendor's POST and this script's own POST to fire -- harmless since both are non-mutating at those statuses.

sapience_notes.subject: Never classify a delegated subprocess's outcome by parsing its stdout/stderr
sapience_notes.value: sapience-project-bind.sh's delegate_link() redirects the vendor CLI's entire stdout and stderr to /dev/null unconditionally. Classification of the delegation outcome is by exit code and by the written link file's own JSON content only -- never by matching against the vendor's English prose, which carries no stability contract and could change wording across vendor versions without notice.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh deployed-mode smoke check vs. authoritative source-store check (carried forward from Phases 1-2)
sapience_notes.value: bash .claude/scripts/verify-touched.sh in this repo runs run-all.sh in its default 'deployed' mode, which executes the deployed, pre-edit copy of a suite whenever that extension's deployed .claude/ mirror is stale -- reconfirmed this phase: the deployed test-sapience-project-bind.sh still lacked cases 22-24 even though the narrowed verify-touched.sh run reported green (it was running the stale 21-case deployed file). The authoritative check for a source-store edit under this condition remains the direct CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store invocation of the suite from its source-store path, which this phase confirmed green at 24 cases / 61 assertions.
